raw_response:
I'm 65 now, and I've been farming this same plot for 40 years. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, so most days it's just me and my old man in the fields. They send some money home every month, but I still watch every yuan — you never know when someone gets sick or the pump breaks.

I'll plant maize in late April, same as I always do. I buy hybrid seed from Old Wang's shop in the village for about 40 yuan per mu. I don't save my own seed anymore; I learned maybe 20 years ago that the ears come out small and half-empty the second year.

For fertilizer, I do what worked last year. I buy one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer and spread it all on my 1.5 mu before planting. Then I buy half a bag of urea — 25kg — and sprinkle it when the maize is knee-high. I know some folks put more, but fertilizer is dear and my son's wages don't leave much extra. Last year my neighbor Chen tried using less and his maize turned yellow before harvest, so I'm not cutting back either. Better to spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing the crop.

I'll irrigate twice from the well — once after planting if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out. Pumping costs electricity, so I don't water more unless it's a drought year. I'll spray herbicide once after planting because at my age I can't bend down pulling weeds all day. If I see armyworms, I'll spray insecticide too.

I don't hire labor for 1.5 mu. My husband and I do everything ourselves, though it takes us longer now than it did ten years ago. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the rain is normal. That's not big money, but it's enough for our own food and some pocket change.
